ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Eight congruent equilateral triangles, each of a different color, are used to construct a regular octahedron. How many distinguishable ways are there to construct the octahedron? (Two colored octahedrons are distinguishable if neither can be rotated to look just like the other.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram depicts a regular octahedron, a solid made from 8 triangular faces. Some edges are dotted to indicate hidden/back edges, consistent with the 3D octahedron structure. Reasoning: The problem asks for colorings of the 8 faces using 8 distinct colors, where two colorings are considered the same if one can be rotated to match the other. There are 8! raw assignments of the 8 distinct colors to the 8 faces. The rotational symmetry group of a regular octahedron has 24 rotations. By Burnside's lemma, we average the number of colorings fixed by each rotation. The identity rotation fixes all 8! colorings. Any non-identity rotation moves at least one face to a different face; since all colors are distinct, a coloring cannot remain unchanged under such a move. Therefore every non-identity rotation fixes 0 colorings. Thus the number of distinguishable colored octahedrons is 8!/24 = 40320/24 = 1680.

method.method_draft: Use Burnside's lemma on face colorings. From the text, note that the eight triangular faces receive eight distinct colors and colorings equivalent under rotations are identified. From the image/text, identify the solid as a regular octahedron with 8 faces. Count all raw assignments as 8!. Use the fact that the rotational symmetry group of a regular octahedron has 24 elements. Because all 8 colors are distinct and every face has a unique color, no non-identity rotation can fix a coloring: any nontrivial rotation moves at least one face to a different face, forcing two different colors to coincide if the coloring were fixed. Thus Burnside gives (8! + 0 + ... + 0)/24 = 8!/24 = 1680.

method.method_draft: Count by opposite face pairs. From the octahedron structure, its 8 faces form 4 pairs of opposite faces. Since rotations preserve opposition, first decide which colors are opposite each other: partition the 8 distinct colors into 4 unordered pairs, giving 8!/(2^4 4!) = 105 possibilities. For any fixed pairing of colors, the four opposite face-pair positions of the octahedron can be permuted arbitrarily by rotations, so assigning the four color-pairs to the four geometric opposite-face pairs contributes no extra distinguishable factor. Once the pairs are placed, choose which color of each pair goes on which of the two opposite faces: 2 choices per pair, hence 2^4 = 16 choices. Therefore the total is 105 · 16 = 1680.
